comment: MEASURED (suite source AbstractVerifyScopesReturnedInClaims.java): the condition requires userinfo to carry ALL 14 profile standard claims (name, given_name, family_name, middle_name, nickname, profile, picture, website, gender, birthdate, zoneinfo, locale, updated_at, preferred_username) whenever `profile` is requested. The user model holds only `name`, and OIDC Core 5.3.2 forbids null/empty placeholders, so this warning is honest until the profile model grows. THE-CONSENTED-SCOPE gated `name` under the profile scope; that does not change this condition.

FINDING surfaced by THE-CONSENTED-SCOPE, recorded not fixed: the module requests `name` through the `claims` request parameter ({"userinfo":{"name":{"essential":true}}}) with scope=openid only. The OP does not support the claims parameter (discovery omits claims_parameter_supported, i.e. false; OIDC Core 5.5 makes support OPTIONAL) and releases `name` only under the consented `profile` scope per the owner ruling. It passed before only because `name` was served unconditionally. Honoring individual claim requests needs consent-of-claims (authorize parsing, code-row persistence, consent page) — own slice.

DELIBERATE posture, not a defect: the OP stamps the session's REAL acr and refuses to echo a requested acr_values it did not perform — faking authentication context would be worse than this warning (acr is a voluntary claim).

FINDING, recorded not fixed (security-relevant SHOULD, RFC 6749 4.1.2): replaying a consumed code refuses the exchange but does NOT revoke the access token minted at the first exchange. MEASURED root cause: the AuthCodeReuseRevoker seam has zero production implementations and zero production wiring, and precise revocation needs the exchange to record the minted access JTI on the code row (own slice).
